newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to decide on Schiphol night ban by early Aug.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to decide on Schiphol night ban by early Aug.

text.p: A government decision on controversial restrictions to keep noise levels at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport within legal limits is expected early next month, the transport ministry said on Wednesday.
Schiphol's proposed ban on night flights for most wide-body aircraft and non-scheduled services from August 1 has run into strong opposition from both domestic and foreign airlines.
"These are complicated proposals which must first be assessed... a decision by (transport) minister (Annemarie Jorritsma) will come some time early next month," ministry spokesman Henk Houtman said.
But a firm decision was unlikely before the August 1 date set by Schiphol for implementation of the proposals, he added.
Representatives from the airline industry, government and civil aviation authority attended a public hearing on the proposals earlier on Wednesday.
Dutch carrier KLM, Schiphol's biggest user, said the proposed restrictions were too stringent and could be relaxed without breaking legal noise limits.

"Reactions from Schiphol users to the proposed measures show that these will likely involve far-reaching consequences for them...this information will be taken into account in assessing the proposed measures," the ministry said in a statement.
